concept_purpose: Eco's 'semiological guerrilla warfare' theorizes tactical, decoding-side resistance to dominant media messages from below.
paper_title: Ambushing the Indian Screen: Vernacularisation, Semiotic Tactics and Magical Realism
journal: BioScope: South Asian Screen Studies
paper_argument: Reads Om Dar-B-Dar and Ghode Ko Jalebi Khilane Le Ja Riya Hu as avant-garde/prayoga films that deploy vernacular 'semiotic guerrilla tactics' to ambush dominant cinematic codes and circulate a localized magic realism.

concept_purpose: Jameson theorized magic realism as a formal mode registering the collision of pre-capitalist and modern modes of production in (semi-)peripheral societies.
paper_title: Ambushing the Indian Screen: Vernacularisation, Semiotic Tactics and Magical Realism
journal: BioScope: South Asian Screen Studies
paper_argument: Recovers an obscure vernacular history of magic realism's circulation in India, arguing it constituted the affective communities and avant-garde milieu the two films draw on.

concept_purpose: Pinney's work on vernacular/'corpothetic' visual culture explains how Indian popular images are made and used outside elite art-historical frames.
paper_title: Ambushing the Indian Screen: Vernacularisation, Semiotic Tactics and Magical Realism
journal: BioScope: South Asian Screen Studies
paper_argument: Uses Pinney's vernacular-image framework to anchor the films' postcolonial vernacularisation of magic realism in Indian popular visual practice.

concept_purpose: Derrida's hauntology names how the past (and the unresolved) returns to disrupt the present as a spectral, never-settled presence.
paper_title: Gender Hauntings at the Border: Qissa's Narration of Partition Through the Trans Body
journal: BioScope: South Asian Screen Studies
paper_argument: Argues that Qissa's spiral, ghost-possession structure stages the Partition's unresolved trauma as gendered hauntings, with male ghosts possessing female bodies to figure the transitivity of gender, nation and genre.

concept_purpose: Trans studies theorizes the trans body as a site that destabilizes naturalized gender, exposing the violence of imposed binary regimes.
paper_title: Gender Hauntings at the Border: Qissa's Narration of Partition Through the Trans Body
journal: BioScope: South Asian Screen Studies
paper_argument: Reads the patriarch's imposition of masculinity on his daughter and the film's gender shape-shifting as a folkloric, fluid trans embodiment responding to Partition's border violence.

theorist: Daniel Dayan & Elie Katz (reworked toward affect)
concept_purpose: The 'media event' concept theorizes how broadcast ceremonies/ruptures are constructed and ritually staged to constitute publics.
paper_title: Anatomy of a Media Event: Disinformation and Event Making in Television and Social Media
journal: BioScope: South Asian Screen Studies
paper_argument: Argues that disinformation is not separate information but is distributed affectively as part of media events; using the Praveen Nettar assassination he shows how television and social media 'event-making forms' produce communal affective politics in India.

concept_purpose: Affect theory explains how pre-cognitive intensities circulate through media to mobilize bodies and political feeling.
paper_title: Anatomy of a Media Event: Disinformation and Event Making in Television and Social Media
journal: BioScope: South Asian Screen Studies
paper_argument: Treats media events as affective spaces whose event-making forms signify politics to audiences, locating disinformation within a network of affective rather than purely informational circulation.

theorist: Concept developed by Dootson & Gaur (engaging media materiality / trace)
concept_purpose: Reorients colour-film historiography from extant images toward material traces (music, ephemera, oral history) to write histories of lost films.
paper_title: A History of Colour Cinema That Can Account for Indian Cinema: The Bombay Film Laboratory, Kashmir's Climate and Gevacolor's Pamposh
journal: BioScope: South Asian Screen Studies
paper_argument: Argues the lost film Pamposh survives in non-filmic traces that reveal how the assimilation of Gevacolor into Bombay cinema became a paradigm for the political assimilation of Kashmir into India.

concept_purpose: Theorizes the nation as an imagined community continuously codified through cultural production, monuments and anniversaries.
paper_title: A Looking Glass War: Bangladesh's Pendulum-swing Liberation War Cinema
journal: BioScope: South Asian Screen Studies
paper_argument: Reads two Liberation War films made 40 years apart (Ora Egaro Jon, Meherjaan) to trace a 'pendulum-swing' centring, decentring and return of the 1971 war as the singular event grounding Bangladeshi national identity.

concept_purpose: Dyer's star theory analyzes the star as an ideologically constructed text that negotiates social tensions around identity and desire.
paper_title: At the Crossroads of Erotic and Mainstream: The Two-phase Celebrity Stardom of Silk Smitha in Malayalam Cinema
journal: BioScope: South Asian Screen Studies
paper_argument: Argues Silk Smitha's two-phase erotic-mainstream star text subverts, substantiates and reinstates the cultural myth of the ideal Malayali feminine, reconfiguring glamour, sexuality and female stardom in Kerala.

concept_purpose: Chiang coined 'transtopia' for a discursive space that shifts debate from what transgender 'is' to what it 'can do' across cultures.
paper_title: Toward a cinematic transtopia
journal: Journal of Chinese Cinemas
paper_argument: Argues that despite near-invisibility of trans self-representation in Chinese independent film, Zhang Wei's The Rib (2019) fosters a visible 'transtopia' reconfiguring trans subjectivity.

concept_purpose: Shih's 'Sinophone' reframes Chinese-language production from the margins against Han-centrism and Chinese imperial centrality.
paper_title: Queering the cinematic border of the PRC and Hong Kong: On Fruit Chan's prostitute trilogy
journal: Journal of Chinese Cinemas
paper_argument: Argues Fruit Chan's sex-worker trilogy uses a Sinophone analytic of 'queering borders' to challenge the boundary of Chinese cinema across colonial legacy, nationalism and Hong Kong localism.

concept_purpose: Affect theory explains how feeling circulates between bodies and images to forge collective attachments outside dominant norms.
paper_title: Queering community: The affect of visuality in the Sinosphere
journal: Journal of Chinese Cinemas
paper_argument: Argues the activist couple Shitou and Mingming's photographs/documentaries construct an 'affective feminist vision' that becomes a community-making practice resisting Han-centric heteronormative norms.

concept_purpose: Theorizes how diasporic queer subjects use media to articulate intersectional, transnational identity and politics.
paper_title: Digital video activism: Fan Popo's queer Asian diasporic politics
journal: Journal of Chinese Cinemas
paper_argument: Argues Fan Popo's post-2017 Berlin filmmaking enacts a context-specific, transversal queer politics rooted in a queer Asian diaspora subject position.

concept_purpose: Chion's 'acousmatic' names sound heard without seeing its source, theorizing how cinema decouples sound from image to structure listening and power.
paper_title: Hou Hsiao-hsien's acousmatic sound: Listening to urban noises and decadent music in Daughter of the Nile
journal: Journal of Chinese Cinemas
paper_argument: Argues Daughter of the Nile (1987) builds acousmatic urban soundscapes implying an 'ethics of listening' that exposes power dynamics amid 1980s Taiwan noise-control debates.

theorist: Anatoly Detwyler (theorizing an indigenous Chinese concept)
concept_purpose: Re'nao names the embodied, participatory immersion of an active crowd, set against the alienated individual gaze of modern spectatorship.
paper_title: Shanghai Fever: Speculation and spectatorship in the 'hot noise' of postsocialist China
journal: Journal of Chinese Cinemas
paper_argument: Argues Shanghai Fever (1994) dramatizes the friction between participatory re'nao and modern spectatorship within postsocialist China's speculative economy.

concept_purpose: Agamben's 'bare life' names life stripped to mere biological existence and exposed to sovereign power.
paper_title: From bare life to still life: Knife in the Clear Water
journal: Journal of Chinese Cinemas
paper_argument: Argues Knife in the Clear Water (2016) exposes the limits of 'bare life' for ethnic-minority precarity by reorienting the concept toward the 'bareness' of the arid land itself as a vital life form.

concept_purpose: Combines Shih's peripheral Sinophone with Nichols's performative documentary mode to read filmmaker-intervention and melancholic affect.
paper_title: Blue, as in 'melancholy': Blue Island and Sinophone performativity
journal: Journal of Chinese Cinemas
paper_argument: Argues Chan Tze-woon's Blue Island (2022) stages a melancholic, performative re-enactment of Hong Kong's struggles, recasting the Sinophone as a wider decolonial practice.

concept_purpose: Alaimo's transcorporeality theorizes the body as porous and materially interconnected with environment.
paper_title: Somatic intermediality: Bodies, environment and population policies in Chinese children's science fiction films (1988-1992)
journal: Journal of Chinese Cinemas
paper_argument: Argues children's bodies in late-1980s/early-1990s sci-fi films function as a 'biosemiotic index' where China's population-control, cybernetic and environmental anxieties converge.

concept_purpose: Names how socialist political truths were rendered as immediate and affective as natural forces, theorizing affect in propaganda aesthetics.
paper_title: Documentary art film and affective truth: Genre hybridity, the combination of revolutionary realism and revolutionary romanticism, and elemental ideology in socialist China
journal: Journal of Chinese Cinemas
paper_argument: Argues the Great Leap Forward's 'documentary art film' genre hybridized documentary and fiction to forge an affective, corporeal link to 'historical truth' under the 2RR principle.

concept_purpose: Rothberg's 'implicated subject' names those neither victims nor perpetrators but entangled in and benefiting from historical injustice.
paper_title: Present perfect cinema and the implicated subject: the utilization of photographs in Oshima Nagisa's Diary of Yunbogi
journal: Journal of Japanese and Korean Cinema
paper_argument: Argues Oshima positions himself as a Japanese 'implicated subject' who asserts solidarity as a citizen of the former colonizing state, linking Japan and South Korea through shared American occupation.

concept_purpose: Williams's 'structure of feeling' captures the shared, not-yet-articulated affective texture of a historical present.
paper_title: Recessionary cinema in post-bubble Japan
journal: Journal of Japanese and Korean Cinema
paper_argument: Argues Yamashita Nobuhiro's films register the 'structure of feeling' of post-bubble Japan, an affective residue of financial precarity beneath everyday life rendered through slow aesthetics.

theorist: Jean-Louis Baudry (re-mediated by Theresa Hak Kyung Cha)
concept_purpose: 1970s apparatus theory analyzes how the cinematic apparatus ideologically constructs the viewing subject.
paper_title: Theresa Hak Kyung Cha as a re-mediating theoretician-artist: Apparatus (1981), Maya Deren, and the genealogy of women's media art
journal: Journal of Japanese and Korean Cinema
paper_argument: Argues Cha absorbed and transformed 1970s apparatus theory through her edited volume Apparatus (1981) into a trans-medial mode of theorization, building a genealogy of women's media art.

concept_purpose: Krauss's 'post-medium condition' names contemporary art no longer defined by a single medium's specificity but operating across media.
paper_title: Theresa Hak Kyung Cha as a re-mediating theoretician-artist: Apparatus (1981), Maya Deren, and the genealogy of women's media art
journal: Journal of Japanese and Korean Cinema
paper_argument: Argues Cha's ritualistic art exemplifies a post-medium condition reactivating media's sensory and affective dimensions beyond medium specificity.

concept_purpose: Film phenomenology theorizes viewing as a bodily, sensorial encounter producing moral and affective response.
paper_title: Not even human: empathy and ambiguity in Park Chan-wook's Judgement and Sympathy for Mr. Vengeance
journal: Journal of Japanese and Korean Cinema
paper_argument: Argues that through techniques of embodiment and alienation Park draws viewers into moral judgment while denying them a stable ethical position.

concept_purpose: Theorizes the hegemonic Japanese male ideal of the corporate male breadwinner and how it organizes gender roles.
paper_title: Gokushufudo drama from a gender perspective: negotiating salaryman masculinity and affirming the gendered division of labour in Japanese society
journal: Journal of Japanese and Korean Cinema
paper_argument: Argues the househusband protagonist negotiates salaryman masculinity while the drama ultimately affirms the persistent split between paid labour and unpaid domestic work.

concept_purpose: The 'division film' genre theorizes how Korean cinema mediates the trauma and politics of national partition.
paper_title: Shiri and the transformation of division films in South Korea's Post-Cold War era
journal: Journal of Japanese and Korean Cinema
paper_argument: Argues that under the 1998 Sunshine-Policy regime division films shifted from propaganda to commercial cinema, with Shiri (1999) blending melodrama and action to balance realism and melodramatic fantasy.

keyword: film noir as mode vs. genre
concept_purpose: Distinguishes genre (industrial category) from mode (transhistorical sensibility) to explain how a national cinema appropriates an imported form.
paper_title: The dark line of Japanese noir: generic appropriation, Matsumoto Seicho, and Nomura Yoshitaro's Stakeout (1958)
journal: Journal of Japanese and Korean Cinema
paper_argument: Argues that by conflating genre and mode, Nomura's Stakeout transcends noir-as-subgenre to form an alternative 'line' of Japanese films intertwining social, cultural and national media discourses.

concept_purpose: Auge coined 'non-place' for the transient, anonymous spaces of supermodernity that lack relational, historical or identitary anchoring.
paper_title: Between the global and the national: Reading place and non-place in El hombre de al lado/The Man Next Door
journal: Studies in Spanish & Latin American Cinemas
paper_argument: Uses Auge's place/non-place distinction to read the neighbours' conflict over the Curutchet House as a tension between the global and the national encoding competing modes of belonging.

concept_purpose: Cultural-memory and trauma theory explain how unprocessed collective traumas persist and structure later individual and national identity.
paper_title: As if Franco had never existed? The intrusive past in Pedro Almodovar's Tacones lejanos/High Heels
journal: Studies in Spanish & Latin American Cinemas
paper_argument: Argues the film's flashbacks stage an inescapable Francoist past, using individual childhood trauma as an analogy for how 1990s Spain under the 'Pact of Forgetting' still had to confront its dictatorial history.

concept_purpose: Postmemory/material-memory explains how children of the disappeared remember a traumatic past via engagement with material traces.
paper_title: Haunting photographs and temporal landscapes: Remembering through traces in La idea de un lago/The Idea of a Lake
journal: Studies in Spanish & Latin American Cinemas
paper_argument: Reads the Argentine film's photographs and landscape as 'material memory' embodying the children-of-the-disappeared's relation to an absent parent, reinforcing Kirchnerist memory politics.

concept_purpose: Ahmed's queer phenomenology theorizes how bodies are oriented in space and how queer disorientation reorganizes the experience of space.
paper_title: Oblique desires: Late-Francoist Spanish Fantaterror according to queer phenomenology
journal: Studies in Spanish & Latin American Cinemas
paper_argument: Applies queer phenomenology to 1969-74 fantaterror mise-en-scene, arguing the queer construction of cinematic space diagnoses the transitional crisis of the late-Francoist film industry and regime.

concept_purpose: Puar mobilizes 'assemblage' to theorize identity/sexuality/race as fluid, intersecting configurations rather than stable categories.
paper_title: Love that dares speak its femininity: Trans* representation in Brazil
journal: Studies in Spanish & Latin American Cinemas
paper_argument: Uses Puar's assemblage with trans theory and Black feminism to argue the short film renders a trans*/travesti sex-worker's femininity in a complex, non-reductive way.

concept_purpose: 'Slow cinema' theorizes a contemplative aesthetic (long takes, minimal narrative) resisting accelerated capitalist time.
paper_title: Dystopian Contra-Futurismos: Subtle science fiction meets slow cinema in Dead Slow Ahead (Herce 2015) and Jauja (Alonso 2014)
journal: Studies in Spanish & Latin American Cinemas
paper_argument: Argues juxtaposing slow cinema with concealed sci-fi produces a 'counter-futurism': Dead Slow Ahead critiques capitalist exploitation while Jauja interrogates colonialism and cosmic time.

concept_purpose: Mouffe's agonism theorizes ineradicable political antagonism; Berlant's affect theory explains attachment to a damaging present ('cruel optimism').
paper_title: Mobilizing affect in Spanish film and screen media from the Great Recession to the present (special issue introduction)
journal: Studies in Spanish & Latin American Cinemas
paper_argument: Frames the special issue's analyses through affect theory and Mouffe's agonism/'the passions', reading post-Recession Spanish screen media as sites of antagonistic political feeling.

concept_purpose: Rocha's 'estetica da fome' argues the authentic art of the colonized Third World expresses violence and deprivation rather than aestheticizing them.
paper_title: The aesthetics of childhood hunger and dreams in contemporary Indian cinema: Representation of children in Sahaj Paather Gappo, Kaaka Muttai and Stanley Ka Dabba
journal: Studies in South Asian Film & Media
paper_argument: Reading three Indian films through Rocha's aesthetics of hunger, argues they render class-, caste- and gender-based marginalization of children visible as everyday resistance against capitalist amnesia.

concept_purpose: Freud's psychoanalytic theory of love and sexuality explains how unconscious drives and infantile sexuality structure adult erotic life.
paper_title: Margarita with a Straw: Laila's queer liberation
journal: Studies in South Asian Film & Media
paper_argument: Reads the disabled bisexual protagonist Laila through Freudian concepts of perversion, narcissism and homoeroticism, arguing her queer-feminist self ultimately transcends classical Freudian frameworks.

concept_purpose: The cultural-imperialism thesis explains how dominant media flows homogenize and subordinate local cultures, eroding their autonomy.
paper_title: Singing Kokborok, dancing Bollywood: Neo-Bollywoodized Tripuri identities and indigenizing the global in contemporary Kokborok music videos
journal: Studies in South Asian Film & Media
paper_argument: Argues Kokborok music videos' 'Bollywoodization' produces hybrid neo-Bollywoodized subjectivities that internalize and reinscribe the very metropolitan gaze they appear to resist.

concept_purpose: Bhabha's hybridity explains how colonial encounters produce an ambivalent 'third space' of mixed, unstable identities capable of mimicry and subversion.
paper_title: Singing Kokborok, dancing Bollywood: Neo-Bollywoodized Tripuri identities and indigenizing the global in contemporary Kokborok music videos
journal: Studies in South Asian Film & Media
paper_argument: Uses hybridity to theorize a 'double indigenizing/double fetishizing' of Tripuri culture, arguing the videos' commercial hybridity risks attenuating Tripuri indigeneity.

concept_purpose: Cinematic cartography theorizes how film maps and produces urban space, scale and atmosphere rather than merely recording it.
paper_title: Bombay cinema's mapping impulse: Location, suspense and atmosphere
journal: Studies in South Asian Film & Media
paper_argument: Argues that through suspense films like Ugly, Trapped and Badla, production infrastructures and vertical/horizontal/atmospheric urbanism generate a 'cartographic diversity' in contemporary Indian cinema's spatial imagination.

concept_purpose: Poole's 'visual economy' analyzes how images circulate within a transnational system of production, exchange and value linked to political-economic power.
paper_title: 'I am in love, I am in love, I am in looove!': The visual economy of the Indo-Swiss-film-tourism complex around 2000
journal: Studies in South Asian Film & Media
paper_argument: Reads the Indo-Swiss film-tourism complex (the Yash Chopra suite at Viktoria Jungfrau) as a 'visual economy' producing a composite cross-cultural style in visual and design culture.
